name: an asymmetric dark grey-black crack: one long wandering diagonal stem with a single short side branch on one side and a tiny spur on the other, a short dirt-filled opening along the stem and lit lips under its flatter stretches, drawn as a transparent decal on old asphalt
label: wasteland_ruins/road-crack-b

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: asphalt patch with crack decal, seen from above

answer.evidence: The image is a flat square patch of grey asphalt (rows 0-47, width 48) with a dark crack decal and lighter patches, bordered by brown dirt. The column scans show no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical front face. Only a thin dark strip at rows 44-46 along the bottom, which reads as the dirt border. The object lies flat and is seen from above, which is correct for a flat floor decal. It has no front face, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's outline is tinted (only 5% of dark edge pixels are neutral), so it does not have the sticker look. The measured facts are mixed. It has 7 visible tones per tile, equal to the paving reference and above the grass reference's 3. Its near-flat coverage is 15%, against 0% for both references. By eye, the asphalt base is a mostly even grey-brown with sparse speckle. The crack is thin and has only about 4 lightness steps: dark stem, dirt fill, lit lip and base. Next to the paving reference, where every stone is shaded individually, it reads flatter and thinner. The whole palette is only 11 colours, so the grain and lip highlights are limited. With flat patches remaining and shading shallower than the references, a careful artist would likely not accept it as equal, so it fails on the 'when in doubt' rule.
